decisions.reason: Despite two years without website visibility, this was launched as a flagship tied to the firm's sustainability direction, so sunk investment and public commitment still make management inclined to give it more time and blame weak results on niche-market timing.

As a multi-model foldable container line in the core reusable-packaging business, it is the kind of offering management is likely to continue backing and interpret the missing website presence as portfolio consolidation rather than a clear signal to exit.

With only modest original visibility and no observation for 2020-2021, the stackable crate now has weaker justification under escalation of commitment and is easier to discontinue in favor of established lines or new projects.

The rackable pallet fits the core business but lacked strong public prominence, and after several years without visible support management can more readily release resources from it while still preserving face.

Its stand-alone launch and close fit to the firm's logistics-efficiency promise sustain managerial attachment, so even with fading visibility the firm would narrowly lean toward retaining it for another year rather than admitting failure.
